introduction.definition: A dissolved air flotation (DAF) unit removes suspended solids, oil and grease from water. A recycle stream of clarified water is pressurised and saturated with air. When the pressure is released in the tank, micro-bubbles form and attach to the flocs, floating them to the surface, where a skimmer removes the float as sludge.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Air-to-solids ratio (A/S, typically ~ 0.005–0.06) controls float performance.

pressure.title: Pressure release creates micro-bubbles
pressure.description: Part of the clarified water is pumped to the saturator at about 4–6 bar, where air dissolves into it (Henry's law: more gas dissolves at higher pressure). At the release valve the pressure drops to atmospheric and the excess air comes out of solution as micro-bubbles, which attach to flocs and float them to the surface.

video_tutorials.title: Dissolved Air Flotation Unit — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Dissolved Air Flotation Unit.
A dissolved air flotation (DAF) unit removes suspended solids, oil and grease from water.
A recycle stream of clarified water is pressurised and saturated with air.
When the pressure is released in the tank, micro-bubbles form and attach to the flocs, floating them to the surface, where a skimmer removes the float as sludge.
Typical applications include industrial wastewater (food, dairy, refinery, paper); algae removal in drinking water; oily water treatment.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Recycle Pump (pressurises clarified water), Recycle Pump (pressurises clarified water) — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Dissolved Air Flotation Unit works.
Flocculated feed enters the contact zone.
The recycle pump pressurises water into the saturator.
Pressure release forms micro-bubbles.
Bubbles float the flocs into a surface layer.
The skimmer pushes float into the hopper.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Part of the clarified water is pumped to the saturator at about 4–6 bar, where air dissolves into it (Henry's law: more gas dissolves at higher pressure).

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Dissolved Air Flotation Unit.
Check bubble quality, float and chemicals.
Clean release nozzles; inspect skimmer chain.
Saturator inspection.
Watch for poor float: solids in effluent. Common cause: low air, poor flocculation.
Watch for nozzle clogging: large bubbles. Common cause: scale/solids.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
